name: Diagnostic Virology
description: Introduction to diagnostic virology – direct and indirect methods, specimens and window period; microscopy – light microscopy, electron microscopy, and fluorescence microscopy in virus identification; methods of virus isolation – cell culture, embryonated egg inoculation and animal inoculation; viral antigen detection - methods, assay characteristics, rapid antigen identification techniques; detection of viral antibodies – methods, role of quantitative measurements, class-specific immunoglobulin detection; viral nucleic acids – amplification, detection and quantitation methods; molecular epidemiology of viral infections – high throughput methods; identifying antiviral resistance – genotypic and phenotypic approaches; quality control in diagnostic virology –internal and external quality control, international standards, and Shewhart control charts.
